decisions.presumes: The ally is fighting a war that is entirely theirs, so a war must be running that the player is not part of.
decisions.evidence: Measured on the balance harness (playCampaign, 209 weeks, democrat/republican/independent x prudent/reckless, seeds balance-0 and balance-1, 12 campaigns, 2,508 weeks); warState none holds in 18.6% of weeks, in 6/12 campaigns (war depends on the world seed, so 6 of the 12 campaigns share one world; the other world has no war at all in the first four years). Reachability: auditReachability on the gated def returns zero unreachable findings (preview-7 third-party war board).
decisions.risk: warState none means some war exists that the player is not in, not specifically the closest friend's war; a closest friend at peace elsewhere would still get this week during a distant war. The stronger reading (the counterpart is a belligerent) is not expressible.

premise.what: The incident is the capitals convening a session about the player without telling it, the diplomatic gathering-against that the week then answers.

Pick the permissive reading rather than strand a critical week.
decisions.risk: The coalition engine reading is the true match; if the owner prefers it, the cost is a roughly two-thirds cut in dealing weeks. Also the existing standing and trust bounds may carry the state on their own.
